predecessors.name: Holy Roman Empire
predecessors.text: the Elbe valley around Meissen and Dresden

successors.name: Electorate of Saxony
successors.text: Frederick IV 'is assigned the Duchy of Saxe-Wittenberg and enters the Saxon electorate' in 1423

ledger.x: 965: the March of Gero is divided and Meissen becomes a new march.
978: Margrave Rikdag takes Merseburg and Zeitz.
983: the Great Slav Rising overruns Zeitz.
985: Eckard I succeeds Rikdag; the Ekkehardiner hold the march until 1046 and Eckard is assassinated in 1002.
1018: the Peace of Bautzen cedes the Milceni land to Poland.
1031: Conrad II recovers the Milceni lands.
1046: Otto of Weimar-Orlamünde becomes margrave; Egbert II follows in 1067.
1076: Egbert renounces the Milceni lands to Vratislaus II of Bohemia.
1089: the Wettin Henry of Eilenburg receives Meissen after Egbert is deposed; Conrad the Great reigns 1123-1156, Otto the Rich 1156-1191, Dietrich the Hard-Pressed 1191-1221.
1243: Henry III takes the Pleissenland in pawn.
1247: the War of the Thuringian Succession opens.
1264: Henry III asserts himself in the Landgraviate of Thuringia.
1264: Meissen gains the bulk of Thuringia from the Ludowingian heritage, the rest becoming the Landgraviate of Hesse.
1423: Meissen merges into the Saxon electorate.

wars.name: Great Slav Rising
wars.outcome: The rising overran the March of Zeitz and other areas.

wars.name: German-Polish War (1002-1018)
wars.outcome: The Peace of Bautzen of 1018 ceded the Milceni region (later Upper Lusatia) to Poland; Conrad II recovered it in 1031.

wars.name: War of the Thuringian Succession
wars.outcome: Henry III of Meissen won most of Thuringia.

certainty.note: The page names no border; every region is a circle or modern area around a named place.
